title: Coherence of the mixed-support cup product
statement: In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), mixed-support cup product is natural in $K$ and $L$, and satisfies the associativity identity on $R\Gamma _c(X,K)\otimes R\Gamma (X,L)\otimes R\Gamma (X,M)$; the unit element $1\in H^0(X,A)$ acts as the identity after the canonical identifications; and the compatibility with the iterate of the cup product and with the identification $R\Gamma _c(X,-)\cong R\Gamma (X,-)$ for a proper $X$ holds.

proof.text:
Work first in the point sheaf category, before applying $\operatorname{Fib}_s$. In the conventions [def-pod-conventions], put $T=La_X^*$, $R=Ra_{X*}$, $F=Ra_{X!}$ and write $P_{K,N}=\operatorname{PF}_{a_X,K,N}$. By [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] the map to prove coherent is
$$\mu_{K,L}=F(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)\circ P_{K,RL}:FK\otimes RL\longrightarrow F(K\otimes L).$$
Its definition supplies the finite-Tor domains, including $RL$, $FK$ and the intermediate tensors; take $K,L,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ throughout. Write $c_{N,Q}:T(N\otimes Q)\simeq TN\otimes TQ$ for [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. All associators and unit identifications below are those of that coherent tensor comparison. This works with completed tensors integrally, rationalized operations at $E$, and common finite stages at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, rather than discrete non-torsion etale sheaves.

source.place: sentences 1–3: the projection/counit construction and tensor conventions

proof.text:
For $u:K\to K'$ and $v:L\to L'$, naturality of $P$ in both variables [fix-prop-projection-formula] and naturality of the counit of $T\dashv R$ [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) give
$$F(u\otimes v)\circ\mu_{K,L}=\mu_{K',L'}\circ(Fu\otimes Rv).$$
Indeed, move $Fu\otimes Rv$ through $P$, obtaining $F(u\otimes T(Rv))$, then use $v\varepsilon_L=\varepsilon_{L'}T(Rv)$. This proves naturality as an equality of the specified maps.

Use [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence](ii),(iv) over $B=s$ for the triple $(a_X,\mathrm{id}_s,\mathrm{id}_s)$ with inputs $(K,N,Q)$, all finite-Tor. The source triple product identifies with $F(K\otimes TN\otimes TQ)$. One iterated inverse projection is $(P_{K,N}^{-1}\otimes1_Q)\circ P_{K\otimes TN,Q}^{-1}$; the other is $P_{K,N\otimes Q}^{-1}$ followed by $1\otimes\kappa_{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id}}$. The latter $\kappa$ is the identity: by (iv) it is the inverse projection for the identity, whose formula in [def-exchange-projection] is the identity counit mate, with identity open-extension comparison. Inverting the equality (the projections are isomorphisms by [fix-prop-projection-formula]) gives
$$F(1_K\otimes c_{N,Q})\circ P_{K,N\otimes Q}=P_{K\otimes TN,Q}\circ(P_{K,N}\otimes1_Q).\tag{P}$$
Thus the needed coherence is in the tensor variables, not merely composition of geometric morphisms. The base and all three morphisms satisfy the separated finite-type hypotheses of the cited theorem.

source.place: sentences 3–5: projection coherence for the triple product

proof.text: Set $N=Q=\mathbf1_s$ in (P). Under the canonical unit identifications, naturality of $P$ in its first variable identifies $P_{K\otimes T\mathbf1_s,\mathbf1_s}$ with $P_{K,\mathbf1_s}$. The unital tensor comparison gives $P_{K,\mathbf1_s}=P_{K,\mathbf1_s}^2$. This map is invertible by [fix-prop-projection-formula], so cancellation yields $P_{K,\mathbf1_s}=1_{FK}$. No unproved unit law for the projection transformation is assumed.

source.place: sentence 5: projection with a unit factor

proof.text:
Write $\eta,\varepsilon$ for the ordinary adjunction unit and counit [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The ordinary cup product is the counit transpose
$$\nu_{L,M}=R((\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_M)c_{RL,RM})\circ\eta_{RL\otimes RM}.$$
Its transpose is exactly
$$\varepsilon_{L\otimes M}\circ T\nu_{L,M}=(\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_M)c_{RL,RM}.\tag{C}$$
To check this, move $T R((\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_M)c)$ through the counit by naturality and then cancel $\varepsilon_{T(RL\otimes RM)}\circ T\eta_{RL\otimes RM}$ by the triangle identity. The ordinary unit is $u:\mathbf1_s\to R\mathbf1_X$, the transpose of $T\mathbf1_s\simeq\mathbf1_X$; the same triangle identity says $\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_X}Tu=1_{\mathbf1_X}$. These formulas use the tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

source.place: sentences 3–5: counit and unit identities entering the two cup products

proof.text:
Expand the two triple products. Naturality of $P$ in $K$ moves $F(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)$ through $P_{K\otimes L,RM}$; (P) then gives
$$\mu_{K\otimes L,M}\circ(\mu_{K,L}\otimes1_{RM})=F(1_K\otimes((\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_M)c_{RL,RM}))\circ P_{K,RL\otimes RM}.$$
For the other parenthesization, naturality in the point variable moves $1_{FK}\otimes\nu_{L,M}$ through $P_{K,R(L\otimes M)}$, leaving
$$\mu_{K,L\otimes M}\circ(1_{FK}\otimes\nu_{L,M})=F(1_K\otimes(\varepsilon_{L\otimes M}T\nu_{L,M}))\circ P_{K,RL\otimes RM}.$$
Equation (C) identifies the two right sides. Restore the canonical associators via [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Naturality used here is precisely that of [fix-prop-projection-formula]. This is the requested associativity on $FK\otimes RL\otimes RM$, with one compact-support factor throughout.

source.place: sentences 3–4: equality of the two parenthesizations

proof.text: For completeness, iterating the ordinary product $\nu$ is unambiguous: transpose either triple composite under $T\dashv R$. Apply (C) to the outer product, then naturality of $c$ to the inner product, and apply (C) once more. Both transposes are $(\varepsilon_L\otimes\varepsilon_M\otimes\varepsilon_N)c^{(3)}$. The two $c^{(3)}$ agree by associativity in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) proves equality. The identical argument with $u$ gives the ordinary left and right unit laws. For the mixed product, the triple identity of the previous step replaces each local change of parentheses. Induct on the number of factors: any binary parenthesization is changed to the right-associated one by rotating its left branch, then its smaller branches. Rotations involving the unique first compact-support factor use the mixed identity, and all other rotations use the ordinary identity just proved. Hence every iterate agrees with that right-associated composite, including the single-factor identity case.

source.place: sentence 3 and statement: compatibility with the iterate of the cup product

proof.text:
Naturality of $P$ in the point variable [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives
$$\mu_{K,\mathbf1_X}(1_{FK}\otimes u)=F(1_K\otimes(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_X}Tu))P_{K,\mathbf1_s}=1_{FK},$$
by the unit calculation in steps 4–5. The class of $u$, namely the adjoint of the identity section of the coefficient unit, is $1\in H^0(X,\Lambda)$. In particular at $\Lambda=A$ this is the unit in the statement. Thus it acts by the identity on the complex and consequently on every cohomology group, after the canonical unit identifications.

Assume now that $X$ is proper. Take the identity compactification $(j,p)=(\mathrm{id}_X,a_X)$ in [def-exchange-projection]. It gives the canonical $F\simeq R$; [fix-prop-projection-formula] identifies $P$ with the ordinary direct-image projection $\pi$ under this comparison. Put $b=(\varepsilon_K\otimes1_{T(RL)})c_{RK,RL}$. The defining formula for $\pi_{K,RL}$ is $R(b)\eta_{RK\otimes RL}$. Consequently the mixed composite transported by $F\simeq R$ is
$$R(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)\,R(b)\,\eta_{RK\otimes RL}=R((\varepsilon_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)c_{RK,RL})\,\eta_{RK\otimes RL}=\nu_{K,L}.$$
This proves compatibility with the specified ordinary cup map, not merely an isomorphism between its endpoints. Naturality of the compactification identification lets it pass through each $F$-image in an iterated product, so the same calculation and induction compare all iterates. No comparison of compact and ordinary supports has been used without properness.

source.place: sentences 6–8: identity compactification and agreement of the cup maps

proof.text: Finally apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ to these equalities. Its tensor comparison is natural and preserves associativity, unit and symmetry by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. By [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] the resulting maps are exactly $R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes R\Gamma(X,L)\to R\Gamma_c(X,K\otimes L)$ of the statement. Hence naturality, associativity, the unit and all iterate identities, and the proper comparison hold in the point coefficient category and on cohomology. Every preceding calculation took place at the chosen coefficient stage with that stage's operations; this last passage does not infer equality of integral morphisms from equality of their separate finite reductions.
